description:
Glimipro 1mg Tablet belongs to a group of medicines called sulfonylureas and is used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults.
It helps control blood sugar levels in people with diabetes thereby preventing serious complications of diabetes such as kidney damage and blindness.
Glimipro 1mg Tablet may be used alone or along with other medicines.
It should be taken just before or with the first meal of the day.
Take it regularly at the same time each day to get the maximum benefit.
Your doctor will decide what dose is best for you and this may change from time to time according to your blood sugar levels.Keep taking Glimipro 1mg Tablet, even if you feel well or your blood sugar levels are controlled.
If you stop it without consulting your doctor, your blood sugar levels could rise to put you at risk of diabetes complications such as kidney damage, blindness, nerve problems, and loss of limbs.
Remember that it is only part of a treatment program that should also include a healthy diet, regular exercise, and weight reduction as advised by your doctor.
Your lifestyle plays a big part in controlling diabetes.The most common side effects of taking Glimipro 1mg Tablet include low blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia).
It is important to have regular meals and always carry a fast-acting source of glucose such as sugary food or fruit juice with you.
Drinking alcohol can also increase your risk of low blood sugar levels and hence should be avoided.
Some people may experience an increase in weight with this medicine.You should not take Glimipro 1mg Tablet if you have type 1 diabetes mellitus, diabetic ketoacidosis (high levels of acid in your blood), or if you have severe kidney or liver disease.
Before taking this medicine, tell your doctor if you have ever had heart disease, thyroid disease, or some hormonal conditions, as it may not be suitable.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.
Your blood sugar levels should be checked regularly and your doctor may also advise blood tests to monitor your blood cell counts and liver function.

faq.question: Does Glimipro 1mg Tablet make you sleepy?
faq.answer: Glimipro 1mg Tablet itself does not cause sleepiness. However, it may cause hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) when used with other anti-diabetes medicine. Because of this you may feel sleepy or have problems in sleeping.

faq.question: Is Glimipro 1mg Tablet safe for kidneys?
faq.answer: Glimipro 1mg Tablet does not affect kidneys in patients with normal kidney function. However, its use should be avoided in patients with severe kidney disease since Glimipro 1mg Tablet is principally eliminated by the kidneys.

faq.question: Does Glimipro 1mg Tablet cause memory loss?
faq.answer: No, it is not known that Glimipro 1mg Tablet causes memory loss. However, the use of Glimipro 1mg Tablet may cause low blood sugar which may cause problems with concentration and reduced alertness.

faq.question: Who should not take Glimipro 1mg Tablet?
faq.answer: Glimipro 1mg Tablet should be avoided by patients who are allergic to it, have severe kidney or liver disease, have G6PD-deficiency (an inherited condition affecting red blood cells) or are due to have surgery. Additionally, patients who are trying to get pregnant, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have insulin-dependent diabetes (type 1 diabetes mellitus) should avoid taking Glimipro 1mg Tablet.

faq.question: How long does it take for Glimipro 1mg Tablet to start working?
faq.answer: Glimipro 1mg Tablet takes about 2 to 3 hours to reduce blood sugar levels. You may not feel any difference, but this does not mean the medicine is not working. Continue taking the medication as directed by your doctor and if you have any concerns, discuss it with your doctor.

faq.question: How long do I need to take Glimipro 1mg Tablet? Can I stop the medication?
faq.answer: Usually, the treatment for diabetes is suggested for a long term. You may have to continue the treatment life long. Glimipro 1mg Tablet only controls the sugar levels but does not cure it. Do not stop taking Glimipro 1mg Tablet without talking to your doctor. If you stop taking Glimipro 1mg Tablet suddenly your diabetes may get worse.

faq.question: What can happen if I take more than the recommended dose of Glimipro 1mg Tablet?
faq.answer: Glimipro 1mg Tablet should be taken strictly as advised by the doctor. Overdose of Glimipro 1mg Tablet may significantly decrease your blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia). If you think you have taken an excess dose and experience a dip in your sugar level, consume enough sugar (e.g., a small bar of sugar cubes, sweet juice or sweetened tea) and inform a doctor immediately. Severe cases of hypoglycemia accompanied by loss of consciousness and coma require immediate medical treatment and admission into hospital.

faq.question: Can you take Glimipro 1mg Tablet on an empty stomach?
faq.answer: No. Taking Glimipro 1mg Tablet on an empty stomach can cause your blood sugar levels to become too low. Low blood sugar can cause dizziness, shaking, anxiety, irritability, a fast heartbeat, and confusion. Therefore, you should always take the medicine with breakfast or the first meal of the day. If you are skipping your meal, then you should also avoid taking Glimipro 1mg Tablet.

faq.question: Can Glimipro 1mg Tablet cause dizziness?
faq.answer: Yes, Glimipro 1mg Tablet can cause dizziness as a side effect. If this happens to you, sit or lie down until the symptoms pass. Always carry some sugary food or fruit juice with you in case you experience dizziness while travelling.

faq.question: What should you not eat while taking Glimipro 1mg Tablet?
faq.answer: It is advisable to avoid foods that are high in saturated and trans fats, instead consume fats from fish and nuts. Control your carbohydrate intake as this directly affects your blood sugar.

faq.question: Is Glimipro 1mg Tablet safe to use?
faq.answer: Yes, Glimipro 1mg Tablet tablet is safe when used as directed by the doctor. However, it may show some side effects. For best results, it should be used in the correct dose and at the same time each day.

faq.question: Can people with diabetes have proteins?
faq.answer: Yes, people with diabetes must include proteins along with other essential nutrients in their daily diet. Proteins are one of the major energy providers among all essential nutrients. Besides, being the building blocks of the human body, proteins break down into glucose to release energy. Unlike carbohydrates, the metabolism of proteins into glucose is much slower. Therefore, the release of energy usually takes a few hours after consumption. Thus, the spike in blood sugar levels might occur after a few hours when you are on a high-protein diet.

faq.question: Are artificial sweeteners good for people with diabetes?
faq.answer: No, artificial sweeteners are not good for people with diabetes. They are composed of chemicals that can cause mild to severe side effects. Thus, it is better to limit or avoid their use as much as you can.

faq.question: Can diabetes cause kidney failure?
faq.answer: Yes, uncontrolled diabetes can cause kidney failure. In the long run, diabetes can affect the kidneys leading to a condition called diabetic nephropathy. Diabetic nephropathy is a condition that is a major cause of kidney failure in patients with diabetes. The best way to prevent damage to kidneys is by keeping diabetes in check, making dietary changes, monitoring sugar levels regularly, getting routine blood tests done, and taking prescribed medications on time.

faq.question: Can diabetes be cured?
faq.answer: Diabetes is a condition that causes changes in your blood glucose levels, which if left uncontrolled, can lead to serious health complications affecting the heart, brain, kidneys, and eyes. However, with simple lifestyle changes, diet, and medications, one can manage their condition and lead a healthy life.

faq.question: Does Glimy 1 Tablet cause memory loss?
faq.answer: No, it is not known that Glimy 1 Tablet causes memory loss. However, the use of Glimy 1 Tablet may cause low blood sugar which may cause problems with concentration and reduced alertness.

faq.question: Who should not take Glimy 1 Tablet?
faq.answer: Glimy 1 Tablet should be avoided by patients who are allergic to it, have severe kidney or liver disease, have G6PD-deficiency (an inherited condition affecting red blood cells) or are due to have surgery. Additionally, patients who are trying to get pregnant, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have insulin-dependent diabetes (type 1 diabetes mellitus) should avoid taking Glimy 1 Tablet.

faq.question: How long does it take for Glimy 1 Tablet to start working?
faq.answer: Glimy 1 Tablet takes about 2 to 3 hours to reduce blood sugar levels. You may not feel any difference, but this does not mean the medicine is not working. Continue taking the medication as directed by your doctor and if you have any concerns, discuss it with your doctor.

faq.question: How long do I need to take Glimy 1 Tablet? Can I stop the medication?
faq.answer: Usually, the treatment for diabetes is suggested for a long term. You may have to continue the treatment life long. Glimy 1 Tablet only controls the sugar levels but does not cure it. Do not stop taking Glimy 1 Tablet without talking to your doctor. If you stop taking Glimy 1 Tablet suddenly your diabetes may get worse.

faq.question: What can happen if I take more than the recommended dose of Glimy 1 Tablet?
faq.answer: Glimy 1 Tablet should be taken strictly as advised by the doctor. Overdose of Glimy 1 Tablet may significantly decrease your blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia). If you think you have taken an excess dose and experience a dip in your sugar level, consume enough sugar (e.g., a small bar of sugar cubes, sweet juice or sweetened tea) and inform a doctor immediately. Severe cases of hypoglycemia accompanied by loss of consciousness and coma require immediate medical treatment and admission into hospital.

faq.question: Can you take Glimy 1 Tablet on an empty stomach?
faq.answer: No. Taking Glimy 1 Tablet on an empty stomach can cause your blood sugar levels to become too low. Low blood sugar can cause dizziness, shaking, anxiety, irritability, a fast heartbeat, and confusion. Therefore, you should always take the medicine with breakfast or the first meal of the day. If you are skipping your meal, then you should also avoid taking Glimy 1 Tablet.

faq.question: Can Glimy 1 Tablet cause dizziness?
faq.answer: Yes, Glimy 1 Tablet can cause dizziness as a side effect. If this happens to you, sit or lie down until the symptoms pass. Always carry some sugary food or fruit juice with you in case you experience dizziness while travelling.

faq.question: What should you not eat while taking Glimy 1 Tablet?
faq.answer: It is advisable to avoid foods that are high in saturated and trans fats, instead consume fats from fish and nuts. Control your carbohydrate intake as this directly affects your blood sugar.

faq.question: Is Glimy 1 Tablet safe to use?
faq.answer: Yes, Glimy 1 Tablet tablet is safe when used as directed by the doctor. However, it may show some side effects. For best results, it should be used in the correct dose and at the same time each day.

faq.question: What is Glipi DM Plus Tablet?
faq.answer: Glipi DM Plus Tablet is a combination of two medicines: Glipizide and Metformin. This medicine is used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). It improves the blood glucose levels in adults when taken along with proper diet and regular exercise. Glipizide lowers the blood glucose levels by increasing the release of insulin from the pancreas. Metformin works by lowering the glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity. This combination is not indicated for the treatment of type 1 DM.

faq.question: What are the possible side effects of Glipi DM Plus Tablet?
faq.answer: The use of Glipi DM Plus Tablet is associated with common side effects like hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level), altered taste, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache and upper respiratory tract infection. Its use can also lead to serious but rare side effects like lactic acidosis. On long-term use, it can also lead to Vitamin B12 deficiency.

faq.question: Can the use of Glipi DM Plus Tablet cause hypoglycemia?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glipi DM Plus Tablet can cause hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level). Symptoms of hypoglycemia include nausea, headache, irritability, hunger, sweating, dizziness, fast heart rate and feeling anxious or shaky. It happens more often if you miss or delay your food, drink alcohol, over-exercise or take other antidiabetic medicine along with it. So, regular monitoring of the blood sugar level is important. Always carry some glucose tablets, honey or fruit juice with you.

faq.question: Can the use of Glipi DM Plus Tablet cause lactic acidosis?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glipi DM Plus Tablet can lead to lactic acidosis. It is a medical emergency which is caused by increased levels of lactic acid in the blood. It is also known as MALA (Metformin associated lactic acidosis). It is a rare side effect associated with the use of metformin and therefore, it is avoided in patients with underlying kidney disease, old age patients or who take large amounts of alcohol. Symptoms of lactic acidosis may include muscle pain or weakness, dizziness, tiredness, feeling of cold in arms and legs, difficulty in breathing, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or slow heart rate. If you have these symptoms, stop taking Glipi DM Plus Tablet and immediately consult your doctor.

faq.question: Can the use of Glipi DM Plus Tablet lead to Vitamin B12 deficiency?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glipi DM Plus Tablet can cause Vitamin B12 deficiency on long-term use. It interferes with absorption of Vitamin B12 in the stomach. If untreated, it may cause anemia and nerve problems and the patient can feel a tingling sensation and numbness in the hands and feet, weakness, urinary problems, change in mental status and difficulty in maintaining balance (ataxia). To avoid such problems, some researchers suggest an intake of Vitamin B12 from outside sources at least once every year.

faq.question: Are there any specific conditions in which Glipi DM Plus Tablet should not to be taken?
faq.answer: The use of Glipi DM Plus Tablet should be avoided in patients with known allergy to any of the components or excipients of this medicine. It should also be avoided in patients with moderate to severe kidney disease and in patients with underlying metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis.

faq.question: Is it safe to take alcohol while I am also taking Glipi DM Plus Tablet?
faq.answer: No, it is not safe to take Glipi DM Plus Tablet along with alcohol, as it may lower your low blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia) and can increase the chances of lactic acidosis.

faq.question: What are the instructions for storage and disposal of Glipi DM Plus Tablet?
faq.answer: Keep this medicine in the container or the pack it came in, tightly closed. Store it according to the instructions mentioned on the pack or label. Dispose of the unused medicine. Make sure it is not consumed by pets, children and other people.

faq.question: What is Prazole DM Capsule used for?
faq.answer: Prazole DM Capsule is used to treat several acid-related stomach and intestinal conditions such as peptic ulcer, gastric ulcer, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It helps relieve heartburn, heals ulcers, and prevents damage caused by excess acid in the stomach and food pipe.

faq.question: How long does Prazole DM Capsule take to work?
faq.answer: Some people begin to feel better within a few days, but it may take up to 4 weeks for full relief. Most ulcers and reflux symptoms heal within 4 to 8 weeks of treatment, depending on your condition.

faq.question: Can I take Prazole DM Capsule every day?
faq.answer: Yes, Prazole DM Capsule can be taken daily as prescribed. However, prolonged or unnecessary use should be avoided. Long-term use may increase the risk of bone fractures, vitamin B12 deficiency, magnesium imbalance, or fundic gland polyps. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration necessary.

faq.question: Can I take Prazole DM Capsule with other medicines?
faq.answer: Some medicines can interact with Prazole DM Capsule. Do not take it with rilpivirine-containing medicines. Avoid combining it with St. John’s Wort or rifampin, as these can reduce its effectiveness. This medicine may also affect the way clopidogrel, warfarin, methotrexate, and digoxin work. Always inform your doctor about all other medicines or supplements you use.

faq.question: Is Prazole DM Capsule safe during pregnancy or while breastfeeding?
faq.answer: Studies have not shown an increased risk of birth defects with Prazole DM Capsule use during pregnancy. It may be used if clearly needed under medical advice. Small amounts may pass into breast milk, but no harmful effects have been reported in infants. Always consult your doctor before use if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.

faq.question: Can I stop taking Prazole DM Capsule once I feel better?
faq.answer: Do not stop taking it suddenly without consulting your doctor. Stopping early may cause your symptoms to return or worsen. Complete the full treatment course as directed.

faq.question: What should I avoid while taking Prazole DM Capsule?
faq.answer: Avoid drinking alcohol, smoking, or eating spicy and fatty foods, as these can worsen acid-related symptoms. Do not take it with rilpivirine or herbal products such as St. John’s Wort, as they may interfere with treatment.

faq.question: What is the best time to take Glipidiab 5 Tablet?
faq.answer: Take Glipidiab 5 Tablet before meals or exactly as instructed by your doctor. There is evidence stating that Glipidiab 5 Tablet works best at controlling post meal high blood sugar levels when taken 30 minutes before breakfast. So, if you are supposed to take it once daily, take it in the morning before breakfast with a glass of water.

faq.question: Is Glipidiab 5 Tablet the same as metformin?
faq.answer: No, Glipidiab 5 Tablet is not the same as metformin. Although both these oral medicines are used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes, the way they work to reduce the sugar levels are different. While Glipidiab 5 Tablet acts by increasing the secretion of insulin by the pancreas, metformin acts by improving the functioning and effectiveness of the insulin already available in the body.

faq.question: Is Glipidiab 5 Tablet bad for kidneys?
faq.answer: No, Glipidiab 5 Tablet is not harmful if your kidney function is normal. faq.question: Does Glipidiab 5 Tablet make you sleepy?

faq.question: Does Glipidiab 5 Tablet cause weight gain?
faq.answer: Yes, Glipidiab 5 Tablet can cause weight gain. It is advisable to closely monitor your diet and do regular exercise while taking this medicine. Avoid skipping your meal as it can cause very low blood sugar levels and you may end up snacking or taking a lot of sugars.

faq.question: Is Glipidiab 5 Tablet a Thiazolidinedione?
faq.answer: No, Glipidiab 5 Tablet is not a Thiazolidinedione, it is a sulfonylurea. However, both are antidiabetic medicines but belong to a different group of medicines.

faq.answer: Glipidiab 5 Tablet should be avoided by patients who are allergic to it, have severe kidney or liver disease, have G6PD-deficiency (an inherited condition affecting red blood cells), or are due to have surgery. Along with that, patients who are trying to get pregnant, are pregnant, or breastfeeding, or have insulin-dependent diabetes (type 1 diabetes mellitus) should also avoid taking Glipidiab 5 Tablet.

faq.question: What can happen if I take more than the recommended dose of Glipidiab 5 Tablet?
faq.answer: Overdose of Glipidiab 5 Tablet may significantly decrease your blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia). If you have taken an excess dose then you should instantly consume enough sugar (e.g., a small bar of sugar cubes, sweet juice or sweetened tea) and inform a doctor immediately. Severe cases of hypoglycemia accompanied by loss of consciousness and coma are cases of medical emergency requiring immediate medical attention.

faq.question: Can I skip Glipidiab 5 Tablet for a few days?
faq.answer: No, Glipidiab 5 Tablet should not be skipped, as it can make your diabetes worse. If, you miss the dose by mistake, take it as soon as you remember.

description:
Glirum Tablet is a medicine used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults.
It belongs to a group of medicines called sulfonylureas and helps control blood sugar levels in people with diabetes.
This helps to prevent serious complications of diabetes like kidney damage and blindness.
Glirum Tablet may be used by itself or along with other medicines.
It should be taken on an empty stomach.
Take it regularly at the same time each day to get the most benefit.
Your doctor will decide what dose is best for you and this may change from time to time according to how it is working.Keep taking this medicine, even if you feel well or your blood sugar levels are controlled.
If you stop it without consulting your doctor, your blood sugar levels could rise and put you at risk of kidney damage, blindness, nerve problems, and loss of limbs.
Remember that it is only part of a treatment program that should also include a healthy diet, regular exercise, and weight reduction as advised by your doctor.
Your lifestyle plays a big part in controlling diabetes.The most common side effects of taking this medicine include hypoglycemia, nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, dizziness, nervousness, tremor, and flatulence.
Make sure you recognize the signs of having low blood glucose levels, such as sweating, dizziness, headache, and shaking, and know how to deal with it.
To prevent this, it's important to have regular meals and always carry a fast-acting source of glucose such as sugary food or fruit juice with you.
Drinking alcohol can also increase your risk of low blood sugar levels and should be avoided.
Some people may find that they put on weight with this medicine.You should not take it if you have type 1 diabetes mellitus, if you have diabetic ketoacidosis (high levels of acid in your blood), or if you have severe kidney or liver disease.
Before taking this medicine, tell your doctor if you have ever had heart disease, thyroid disease, or some hormonal conditions.
It may not be suitable.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.
Your blood sugar levels should be checked regularly and your doctor may also advise blood tests to monitor your blood cell counts and liver function.

faq.question: What is the best time to take Glirum Tablet?
faq.answer: Take Glirum Tablet before meals or exactly as instructed by your doctor. There is evidence stating that Glirum Tablet works best at controlling post meal high blood sugar levels when taken 30 minutes before breakfast. So, if you are supposed to take it once daily, take it in the morning before breakfast with a glass of water.

faq.question: Is Glirum Tablet the same as metformin?
faq.answer: No, Glirum Tablet is not the same as metformin. Although both these oral medicines are used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes, the way they work to reduce the sugar levels are different. While Glirum Tablet acts by increasing the secretion of insulin by the pancreas, metformin acts by improving the functioning and effectiveness of the insulin already available in the body.

faq.question: Is Glirum Tablet bad for kidneys?
faq.answer: No, Glirum Tablet is not harmful if your kidney function is normal. Any previous case of kidney problem should be informed to the doctor, so that the use of Glirum Tablet can be assessed. This is done in order to analyze whether Glirum Tablet can be given or not because it is principally excreted by the kidney. If you have kidney problems you will be started at a lower dose.

faq.question: Does Glirum Tablet make you sleepy?
faq.answer: Glirum Tablet itself does not cause sleepiness. However, it may cause hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) when used with other anti-diabetes medicine. Because of this you may feel sleepy or have problems in sleeping.

faq.question: Does Glirum Tablet cause weight gain?
faq.answer: Yes, Glirum Tablet can cause weight gain. It is advisable to closely monitor your diet and do regular exercise while taking this medicine. Avoid skipping your meal as it can cause very low blood sugar levels and you may end up snacking or taking a lot of sugars.

faq.question: Is Glirum Tablet a Thiazolidinedione?
faq.answer: No, Glirum Tablet is not a Thiazolidinedione, it is a sulfonylurea. However, both are antidiabetic medicines but belong to a different group of medicines.

faq.question: Who should not take Glirum Tablet?
faq.answer: Glirum Tablet should be avoided by patients who are allergic to it, have severe kidney or liver disease, have G6PD-deficiency (an inherited condition affecting red blood cells), or are due to have surgery. Along with that, patients who are trying to get pregnant, are pregnant, or breastfeeding, or have insulin-dependent diabetes (type 1 diabetes mellitus) should also avoid taking Glirum Tablet.

faq.question: What can happen if I take more than the recommended dose of Glirum Tablet?
faq.answer: Overdose of Glirum Tablet may significantly decrease your blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia). If you have taken an excess dose then you should instantly consume enough sugar (e.g., a small bar of sugar cubes, sweet juice or sweetened tea) and inform a doctor immediately. Severe cases of hypoglycemia accompanied by loss of consciousness and coma are cases of medical emergency requiring immediate medical attention.

faq.question: Can I skip Glirum Tablet for a few days?
faq.answer: No, Glirum Tablet should not be skipped, as it can make your diabetes worse. If, you miss the dose by mistake, take it as soon as you remember.

faq.question: What should you not eat while taking Glista 1mg Tablet?

faq.question: Is Glista 1mg Tablet safe to use?

faq.question: Can people with diabetes have proteins?
faq.answer: Yes, people with diabetes must include proteins along with other essential nutrients in their daily diet. Proteins are one of the major energy providers among all essential nutrients. Besides, being the building blocks of the human body, proteins break down into glucose to release energy. Unlike carbohydrates, the metabolism of proteins into glucose is much slower. Therefore, the release of energy usually takes a few hours after consumption. Thus, the spike in blood sugar levels might occur after a few hours when you are on a high-protein diet.

faq.question: Are artificial sweeteners good for people with diabetes?

faq.question: Can diabetes cause kidney failure?
faq.answer: Yes, uncontrolled diabetes can cause kidney failure. In the long run, diabetes can affect the kidneys leading to a condition called diabetic nephropathy. The best way to prevent damage to kidneys is by keeping diabetes in check, making dietary changes, monitoring sugar levels regularly, getting routine blood tests done, and taking prescribed medications on time.

faq.question: Can diabetes be cured?
faq.answer: Diabetes is a condition that causes changes in your blood glucose levels, which if left uncontrolled, can lead to serious health complications affecting the heart, brain, kidneys, and eyes. faq.question: What is Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet?
faq.answer: Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet is a combination of two medicines: Gliclazide and Metformin. This medicine is used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). It improves blood glucose levels in adults when taken along with proper diet and regular exercise. Gliclazide lowers the blood glucose levels by increasing the release of insulin from the pancreas. Metformin works by lowering the glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity. This combination is not indicated for the treatment of Type 1 DM.

faq.question: What are the possible side effects of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet?
faq.answer: The use of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet is associated with common side effects. These side effects may include hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level), altered taste, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache and upper respiratory tract infection. Its use can also lead to serious but rare side effects like lactic acidosis. On long-term use, it can also lead to vitamin B12 deficiency.

faq.question: Can the use of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet cause hypoglycemia?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet can cause hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level). Symptoms of hypoglycemia include nausea, headache, irritability, hunger, sweating, dizziness, fast heart rate and feeling anxious or shaky. It happens more often if you miss or delay your food, drink alcohol, over-exercise or take other antidiabetic medicine along with it. So, regular monitoring of blood sugar level is important. Always keep glucose tablets, honey or fruit juice with you.

faq.question: Can the use of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet cause lactic acidosis?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet can lead to lactic acidosis. It is a medical emergency which is caused by increased levels of lactic acid in the blood. It is also known as MALA (Metformin associated lactic acidosis). It is a rare side effect associated with the use of metformin. It is avoided in patients with underlying kidney disease, old age patients or who take large amounts of alcohol. Symptoms of lactic acidosis may include muscle pain or weakness, dizziness, tiredness, feeling of cold in arms and legs, difficulty in breathing, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or slow heart rate. If you have these symptoms, stop taking Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet and immediately consult your doctor.

faq.question: Can the use of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet lead to Vitamin B12 deficiency?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet can cause vitamin B12 deficiency on long-term use. The deficiency occurs as the medicine interferes with absorption of vitamin B12 in the stomach. If untreated, it may cause anemia and nerve problems and the patient can have tingling sensation and numbness in hands and feet, weakness, urinary problems, change in mental status and difficulty in maintaining balance (ataxia). To avoid such problems, some researchers suggest an intake of vitamin B12 from outside sources at least once every year.

faq.question: Are there any specific conditions in which Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet should not to be taken?
faq.answer: The use of Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet should be avoided in patients with known allergy to any of the component or excipients of this medicine. It is also avoided in patients with moderate to severe kidney disease or with underlying metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis.

faq.question: Is it safe to take alcohol while I am also taking Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet?
faq.answer: No, it is not safe to take alcohol along with Glizid-M 40/500 Tablet. It may lower your low blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia) and can increase the chances of lactic acidosis.

faq.question: Does Gluconorm G 1 Forte Tablet cause low blood sugar levels?

faq.question: Can the use of Gluconorm G2 Tablet PR lead to lactic acidosis?

faq.question: What are the possible side effects of Gluconorm G2 Tablet PR?

Gluconorm-Z XR Forte 60 Tablet should be taken with food.
Take it regularly at the same time each day to get the most benefit.
Your doctor will decide what dose is best for you and this may change from time to time according to how it is working according to your blood sugar levels.Keep taking this medicine, even if you feel well or your blood sugar levels are controlled.
If you stop it without consulting your doctor, your blood sugar levels could rise and put you at risk of kidney damage, blindness, nerve problems and loss of limbs.
Remember that it is only part of a treatment program that should also include a healthy diet, regular exercise, and weight reduction as advised by your doctor.
Your lifestyle plays a big part in controlling diabetes.The most common side effect of Gluconorm-Z XR Forte 60 Tablet are low blood glucose levels (hypoglycemia), constipation, and vomiting.

faq.question: What is Gluconorm-Z XR Forte 60 Tablet?
faq.answer: Gluconorm-Z XR Forte 60 Tablet is a combination of two medicines: Gliclazide and Metformin. This medicine is used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). It improves blood glucose levels in adults when taken along with proper diet and regular exercise. Gliclazide lowers the blood glucose levels by increasing the release of insulin from the pancreas. Metformin works by lowering the glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity. This combination is not indicated for the treatment of Type 1 DM.

faq.question: What are the possible side effects of Gluconorm-Z XR Forte 60 Tablet?
faq.answer: The use of Gluconorm-Z XR Forte 60 Tablet is associated with common side effects. These side effects may include hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level), altered taste, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache and upper respiratory tract infection. faq.question: Can the use of Gluconorm-Z XR Forte 60 Tablet cause hypoglycemia?

faq.question: Can the use of Gluconorm-Z XR Forte 60 Tablet cause lactic acidosis?

faq.question: What is GLUra MP 500 Tablet SR used for?
faq.answer: GLUra MP 500 Tablet SR is used for adults with type 2 diabetes to help lower high blood sugar when diet and exercise are not enough. It combines three components that work together to control sugar levels throughout the day.

faq.question: Who should not take GLUra MP 500 Tablet SR?
faq.answer: Individuals should not take GLUra MP 500 Tablet SR if they are allergic to metformin, pioglitazone, or sitagliptin. faq.question: Can GLUra MP 500 Tablet SR cause pancreatitis (inflamed pancreas)?

faq.question: Is GLUra MP 500 Tablet SR safe if I have heart problems?

faq.question: Can GLUra MP 500 Tablet SR affect my kidneys or require stopping before scans?

faq.question: Can GLUra MP 500 Tablet SR cause low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)?

description:
Glycomet 500 SR tablets are a medication prescribed to help manage type 2 diabetes.
This chronic condition occurs when your body fails to use insulin effectively, resulting in high blood sugar levels.
Effectively managing your blood sugar is a vital part of maintaining good health, and Glycomet 500 SR is designed to help you do just that.
It helps bring your blood sugar down to a safer range, which in turn helps prevent long-term health complications associated with diabetes.
The key active ingredient in Glycomet 500 SR is metformin.
This powerful component works in two important ways to control your blood sugar.
First, it decreases the amount of sugar your liver produces.
Your liver naturally makes sugar, but in people with type 2 diabetes, it can produce too much.
Second, metformin reduces the amount of sugar your body absorbs from the food you eat.
By addressing sugar from both production and absorption, metformin enables your body's insulin to work more efficiently.
The "SR" in the name stands for "Sustained Release," which means the tablet releases the medication slowly over time for a more consistent effect.
It's extremely important to take Glycomet 500 SR tablets exactly as your doctor has prescribed.
Do not change your dose or stop taking the medication without speaking to your doctor first.
These tablets are typically taken with or after a meal, as consuming them with food can help mitigate any potential stomach-related side effects.
Following your doctor's specific instructions for dosage and timing is essential to ensure the medication works safely and effectively to control your blood sugar levels.
Before starting Glycomet 500 SR, it is essential to have an open and honest conversation with your doctor.
Tell them about all your existing medical conditions.
This is especially important if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
You should also let your doctor know about all other medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements you are currently taking.
This allows your doctor to check for any potential interactions and ensures that Glycomet 500 SR is a safe option for your individual health.
Glycomet 500 SR isn't the only medication that uses metformin to manage type 2 diabetes.
You may have heard of or been prescribed other brands that contain the same active ingredient.
These include Glyciphage SR 500 tablets , Gluconorm SR 500 tablets , Obimet SR 500 tablets , Melmet SR 500 tablets , Biciphage SR 500 tablets , and Bigomet SR 500 tablets .
This is common in the pharmaceutical industry, meaning that several different products utilise the same well-established active ingredient for the same medical purpose.

faq.question: How does this medicine help in both diabetes and PCOS when these are different conditions?
faq.answer: In diabetes, the main issue is high blood sugar due to insulin resistance. In Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, insulin resistance also plays a key role and affects hormone balance. Glycomet 500 SR Tablet improves how the body responds to insulin, which helps lower blood sugar in diabetes and can also help regulate hormones and cycles in PCOS.

faq.question: Can this medicine be used if blood sugar levels are only slightly high?
faq.answer: Yes, it may be prescribed even in early stages or prediabetes to improve insulin sensitivity and prevent progression, especially when lifestyle changes alone are not enough.

faq.question: Do I need to continue Glycomet 500 SR Tablet long-term?
faq.answer: Both diabetes and PCOS are long-term conditions. Glycomet 500 SR Tablet is often used for an extended period, but the duration depends on your response, goals, and your doctor’s advice.

faq.question: What makes Glycomet 500 SR Tablet different from other diabetes medicines?
faq.answer: Unlike some medicines that increase insulin levels, this medicine mainly works by improving how the body uses insulin and reducing sugar production in the liver, which makes it a commonly used first-line treatment.

description:
Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR belongs to a category of medicines known as anti-diabetic drugs.
It is a combination of two medicines used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults.
It helps control blood sugar levels in people with diabetes.
Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR should be taken with food.
Take it regularly at the same time each day to get the most benefit.
Your doctor will decide what dose is best for you, and this may change from time to time according to how it is working, according to your blood sugar levels.Keep taking this medicine, even if you feel well or your blood sugar levels are controlled.
If you stop it without consulting your doctor, your blood sugar levels could rise and put you at risk of kidney damage, blindness, nerve problems, and loss of limbs.
Remember that it is only part of a treatment program that should also include a healthy diet, regular exercise, and weight reduction as advised by your doctor.
Your lifestyle plays a big part in controlling diabetes.The most common side effect of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR is low blood glucose levels (hypoglycemia).
Make sure you recognize the signs of having low blood glucose levels, such as sweating, dizziness, headache, and shaking, and know how to deal with them.
To prevent this, it's important to have regular meals and always carry a fast-acting source of glucose, such as sugary food or fruit juice, with you.
Drinking alcohol can also increase your risk of low blood sugar levels and should be avoided.
Other side effects that may be seen on taking this medicine include taste changes, nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, and upper respiratory tract infection.
Some people may find that they put on weight with this medicine.You should not take it if you have type 1 diabetes mellitus, diabetic ketoacidosis (high levels of acid in your blood), or severe kidney or liver disease.
Before taking this medicine, tell your doctor if you have ever had heart disease.
It may not be suitable.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.
Your blood sugar levels should be checked regularly, and your doctor may also advise blood tests to monitor your blood cell counts and liver function.

faq.question: What is Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR?
faq.answer: Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR is a combination of two medicines: glimepiride and metformin. This medicine is used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). It improves blood glucose levels in adults when taken along with a proper diet and regular exercise. Glimepiride lowers the blood glucose levels by increasing the release of insulin from the pancreas. Metformin works by lowering glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity. This combination is not indicated for the treatment of type 1 DM.

faq.question: Can the use of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR lead to lactic acidosis?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR can lead to lactic acidosis. It is a medical emergency that is caused by increased levels of lactic acid in the blood. It is also known as MALA (metformin-associated lactic acidosis). It is a rare side effect associated with the use of metformin, and therefore, it is considered to be harmful for patients with underlying kidney disease, older patients, or those who take large amounts of alcohol. Symptoms of lactic acidosis may include muscle pain or weakness, dizziness, tiredness, a feeling of cold in arms and legs, difficulty in breathing, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, or a slow heart rate. If you have these symptoms, stop taking Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR and consult your doctor immediately.

faq.question: What are the possible side effects of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR?
faq.answer: The use of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR is associated with common side effects like hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level), altered taste, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, and headache. Its use can also lead to serious but rare side effects like lactic acidosis. On long-term use, it can also lead to vitamin B12 deficiency.

faq.question: Can the use of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR lead to Vitamin B12 deficiency?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR can cause Vitamin B12 deficiency on long-term use. It interferes with the absorption of Vitamin B12 in the stomach. If untreated, it may cause anemia and nerve problems and the patient can experience tingling sensation and numbness in hands and feet, weakness, urinary problems, change in mental status and difficulty in maintaining balance (ataxia). To avoid such problems, some researchers suggest an intake of Vitamin B12 from outside sources at least once every year.

faq.question: Can the use of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR cause hypoglycemia?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR can cause hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level). Symptoms of hypoglycemia include nausea, headache, irritability, hunger, sweating, dizziness, fast heart rate, and feeling anxious or shaky. It happens more often if you miss or delay your food, drink alcohol, over-exercise, or take other antidiabetic medicines along with it. So, regular monitoring of the blood sugar level is important. Always keep a quick source of sugar, like glucose tablets, honey, or fruit juice, with you.

faq.question: Is it safe to take alcohol while I am also taking Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR?
faq.answer: No, it is not safe to take Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR along with alcohol, as it may lower your blood sugar levels and lead to hypoglycemia. It can also increase the chances of lactic acidosis.

faq.question: What are the recommended storage conditions for Glycomet-GP 0.5 Tablet PR?
faq.answer: Keep this medicine in the container or the pack it came in, tightly closed. Store it according to the instructions mentioned on the pack or label. Dispose of the unused medicine. Make sure it is not consumed by pets, children, or other people.

Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR belongs to a category of medicines known as anti-diabetic drugs.
It is a combination of two medicines used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults.
It helps control blood sugar levels in people with diabetes.
Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR should be taken with food.
Take it regularly at the same time each day to get the most benefit.
Your doctor will decide what dose is best for you, and this may change from time to time according to how it is working, according to your blood sugar levels.Keep taking this medicine, even if you feel well or your blood sugar levels are controlled.
If you stop it without consulting your doctor, your blood sugar levels could rise and put you at risk of kidney damage, blindness, nerve problems, and loss of limbs.
Remember that it is only part of a treatment program that should also include a healthy diet, regular exercise, and weight reduction as advised by your doctor.
Your lifestyle plays a big part in controlling diabetes.The most common side effect of Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR is low blood glucose levels (hypoglycemia).
Make sure you recognize the signs of having low blood glucose levels, such as sweating, dizziness, headache, and shaking, and know how to deal with them.
To prevent this, it's important to have regular meals and always carry a fast-acting source of glucose, such as sugary food or fruit juice, with you.
Drinking alcohol can also increase your risk of low blood sugar levels and should be avoided.
Other side effects that may be seen on taking this medicine include taste changes, nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, and upper respiratory tract infection.
Some people may find that they put on weight with this medicine.You should not take it if you have type 1 diabetes mellitus, diabetic ketoacidosis (high levels of acid in your blood), or severe kidney or liver disease.
Before taking this medicine, tell your doctor if you have ever had heart disease.
It may not be suitable.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.
Your blood sugar levels should be checked regularly, and your doctor may also advise blood tests to monitor your blood cell counts and liver function.

faq.question: Can Glycomet GP 1 cause kidney problems?
faq.answer: Glycomet GP 1 tablet (a combination of glimepiride and metformin) does not directly cause kidney damage in healthy kidneys, but it should be used with caution in patients with kidney disease and is contraindicated in severe kidney failure.

faq.question: What diet should I follow while taking Glycomet-GP 1 tablets?
faq.answer: Include a variety of cereals, dal, whole grains, vegetables, and fruits in your daily diet. Each meal should consist of a cereal, dal or lean meat, vegetables, and dairy products for balanced nutrients. Use minimal oil when preparing food and mix different types of oils for better health. Eat one fruit daily as a snack, avoid sugary foods and sweets, and eat at regular intervals with 3 main meals and 1-2 snacks in between to maintain stable glucose levels.

faq.question: How many tablets of Glycomet-GP 1 should I take in a day?
faq.answer: The frequency of taking this medicine will be decided by your doctor based on your age, weight, current regimen and comorbidities present. It varies from person to person.

faq.question: When can I take Glycomet-GP 1 tablet?
faq.answer: Take Glycomet-GP 1 tablet as prescribed by the doctor for the prescribed duration. Take with food, as a whole, with a glass of water. Avoid skipping meals as well as medicine.

faq.question: What is the dose of Glycomet Gp 1?
faq.answer: The doctor will decide the specific dose for a specific duration depending on the underlying condition and the patient's response to the treatment. Do not take it endlessly on your own without consulting a doctor.

faq.question: Can I Stop taking Glycomet GP 1 on my own?
faq.answer: No, you should not discontinue the treatment on your own. Keep taking this tablet even if your symptoms improve to help keep the disease under control, as advised by your doctor for the specified duration. Gradual weaning of the medication should be done to avoid adverse effects.

faq.question: What are the uses of the Glycomet GP 1 tablet?
faq.answer: Glycomet GP 1 is used to manage type 2 diabetes mellitus. It helps control blood sugar levels by enhancing insulin action, reducing sugar production in the liver, and decreasing sugar absorption in the intestine. This maintains blood sugar within target range and helps prevent diabetes-related complications such as kidney damage, nerve issues, and eye problems.

faq.question: What are the side effects of the Glycomet GP 1 tablet?
faq.answer: Common side effects may include low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), nausea, stomach upset, dizziness, headache, or weakness. In rare cases, it can lead to weight gain, skin rash, or lactic acidosis (a serious condition caused by excess lactic acid in the blood). If you experience persistent vomiting, muscle pain, severe tiredness, or difficulty breathing, see your doctor immediately.

faq.question: Can Glycomet GP 1 cause low blood sugar?
faq.answer: Yes, Glycomet GP 1 may sometimes cause hypoglycemia (low blood sugar), especially if you skip meals, exercise excessively, or drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Symptoms can include sweating, shakiness, hunger, dizziness, and a rapid heartbeat. Carry a source of sugar, such as glucose tablets or fruit juice, to manage sudden episodes of low blood sugar.

faq.question: Can Glycomet GP 1 be taken during pregnancy or while breastfeeding?
faq.answer: The safety of Glycomet GP 1 during pregnancy and breastfeeding should be carefully assessed by a doctor. Pregnant women might need to switch to insulin if necessary, and breastfeeding mothers should use this medication only if prescribed. Always consult your doctor before starting or continuing this medication if you are pregnant or nursing.

faq.question: Can Glycomet GP 1 be taken alongside other diabetes medications?
faq.answer: Yes, Glycomet GP 1 is often prescribed alongside other antidiabetic medicines or insulin to improve blood sugar management. However, combining medications can increase the risk of hypoglycaemia, so dose adjustments and regular monitoring are essential. Do not take other medicines for diabetes without your doctor’s approval.

faq.question: What is the difference between Glycomet GP1 and Glycomet GP2?
faq.answer: Glycomet GP1 and GP2 mainly differ in the dose of glimepiride. GP1 contains 1 mg of glimepiride, while GP2 contains 2 mg, along with metformin. GP2 is generally prescribed when blood sugar levels are not well controlled with GP1. Using a higher dose without medical advice may increase the risk of low blood sugar. Your doctor will decide the right strength based on your sugar readings.

faq.question: How is Glycomet GP1 different from Glycomet SR?
faq.answer: Glycomet GP1 is a combination of metformin and glimepiride that works to reduce blood sugar. Glycomet SR contains only metformin in a sustained-release form, which releases the medicine slowly and is gentler on the stomach. GP1 is used when a single medicine is not enough to control diabetes. SR is often preferred in early diabetes or for better stomach tolerance. Consult your doctor to know which option suits your condition. Avoid self-medication.

faq.question: Is Gluconorm G1 the same as Glycomet GP1?
faq.answer: Gluconorm G1 and Glycomet GP1 are combination medications used to treat type 2 diabetes. Both contain metformin and glimepiride. faq.question: Can Glycomet GP1 be used for PCOS?
faq.answer: Glycomet GP1 may be prescribed in women with PCOS who have insulin resistance or high blood sugar levels. This medicine should only be used for PCOS if advised by a doctor. Self-medication is not recommended.

faq.question: How is Glycomet GP1 different from Glimidib M1 or GN1?
faq.answer: Glycomet GP1, Glimidib M1, and GN1 are combination medicines used to manage type 2 diabetes. They contain glimepiride and metformin as their active ingredients but differ in formulation, brand, or price. The choice depends on your blood sugar levels and tolerance. Always follow your doctor’s recommendation for the best results. Do not self-medicate.

faq.question: Is Gmer 1 mg the same as Glycomet GP1?
faq.answer: Gmer 1 mg and Glycomet GP1 are anti-diabetic medicines containing glimepiride and metformin. Do not switch between these medicines without medical advice. Your doctor will guide you on the most suitable option.

faq.question: What is Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR?
faq.answer: Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR is a combination of two medicines: glimepiride and metformin. This medicine is used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). It improves blood glucose levels in adults when taken along with a proper diet and regular exercise. Glimepiride lowers the blood glucose levels by increasing the release of insulin from the pancreas. Metformin works by lowering glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity. This combination is not indicated for the treatment of type 1 DM.

faq.question: Can the use of Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR lead to lactic acidosis?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR can lead to lactic acidosis. It is a medical emergency that is caused by increased levels of lactic acid in the blood. It is also known as MALA (metformin-associated lactic acidosis). It is a rare side effect associated with the use of metformin, and therefore, it is considered to be harmful for patients with underlying kidney disease, older patients, or those who take large amounts of alcohol. Symptoms of lactic acidosis may include muscle pain or weakness, dizziness, tiredness, a feeling of cold in arms and legs, difficulty in breathing, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, or a slow heart rate. If you have these symptoms, stop taking Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR and consult your doctor immediately.

faq.question: What are the possible side effects of Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR?
faq.answer: The use of Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR is associated with common side effects like hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level), altered taste, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, and headache. Its use can also lead to serious but rare side effects like lactic acidosis. On long-term use, it can also lead to vitamin B12 deficiency.

faq.question: Can the use of Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR lead to Vitamin B12 deficiency?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR can cause Vitamin B12 deficiency on long-term use. It interferes with the absorption of Vitamin B12 in the stomach. If untreated, it may cause anemia and nerve problems and the patient can experience tingling sensation and numbness in hands and feet, weakness, urinary problems, change in mental status and difficulty in maintaining balance (ataxia). To avoid such problems, some researchers suggest an intake of Vitamin B12 from outside sources at least once every year.

It happens more often if you miss or delay your food, drink alcohol, over-exercise, or take other antidiabetic medicines along with it. So, regular monitoring of the blood sugar level is important. Always keep a quick source of sugar, like glucose tablets, honey, or fruit juice, with you.

faq.question: Is it safe to take alcohol while I am also taking Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR?
faq.answer: No, it is not safe to take Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR along with alcohol, as it may lower your blood sugar levels and lead to hypoglycemia. It can also increase the chances of lactic acidosis.

faq.question: What are the recommended storage conditions for Glycomet-GP 1 Tablet PR?
faq.answer: Keep this medicine in the container or the pack it came in, tightly closed. Store it according to the instructions mentioned on the pack or label. Dispose of the unused medicine. Make sure it is not consumed by pets, children, or other people.

description:
Glycomet Tablet is a medicine used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus.
It helps control blood sugar levels and thus prevents serious complications of diabetes.
It is also used to treat a menstruation-related disorder known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in women.
Glycomet Tablet is best taken with food to avoid nausea and abdominal pain.
You should take it regularly, at the same time each day, to get the most benefit.
You should not stop taking this medicine unless your doctor recommends it.
Your lifestyle plays a big part in controlling diabetes.
Therefore, it is important to stay on the diet and exercise program recommended by your doctor while taking this medicine.The most common side effects of this medicine include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, headache, and loss of appetite.
Some people may develop hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level) when this medicine is taken along with other antidiabetic medicines or alcohol or upon skipping a meal.
Monitor your blood sugar levels regularly while taking it.Before taking this medicine, inform your doctor if you have any kidney, liver, or heart problems.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.
Your doctor will check your kidney function before starting treatment with it.
Avoid excessive alcohol intake while taking it, as this may increase the risk of developing some side effects.

faq.question: How does this medicine help in both diabetes and PCOS when these are different conditions?
faq.answer: In diabetes, the main issue is high blood sugar due to insulin resistance. In Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, insulin resistance also plays a key role and affects hormone balance. Glycomet Tablet improves how the body responds to insulin, which helps lower blood sugar in diabetes and can also help regulate hormones and cycles in PCOS.

faq.question: Can this medicine be used if blood sugar levels are only slightly high?
faq.answer: Yes, it may be prescribed even in early stages or prediabetes to improve insulin sensitivity and prevent progression, especially when lifestyle changes alone are not enough.

faq.question: Do I need to continue Glycomet Tablet long-term?
faq.answer: Both diabetes and PCOS are long-term conditions. Glycomet Tablet is often used for an extended period, but the duration depends on your response, goals, and your doctor’s advice.

faq.question: What makes Glycomet Tablet different from other diabetes medicines?
faq.answer: Unlike some medicines that increase insulin levels, this medicine mainly works by improving how the body uses insulin and reducing sugar production in the liver, which makes it a commonly used first-line treatment.

faq.question: Can I use Glycosmart FB Capsule for sudden shortness of breath?
faq.answer: No. Glycosmart FB Capsule is not a rescue inhaler. It does not work quickly enough to relieve sudden attacks of breathlessness. You should always keep a fast‑acting rescue inhaler handy for sudden breathing problems.

faq.question: Who should not use Glycosmart FB Capsule?

faq.question: What should I tell my doctor before starting Glycosmart FB Capsule?

faq.question: What are the serious side effects of Glycosmart FB Capsule?

faq.question: Does Glycosmart FB Capsule weaken the immune system?
faq.answer: Glycosmart FB Capsule contains budesonide, a type of corticosteroid, which may slightly lower your body’s ability to fight infections. Wash your mouth after each use and contact your doctor if you develop thrush (white patches in your mouth) or a persistent cough.

faq.question: Can using Glycosmart FB Capsule affect my eyes or bones?
faq.answer: Long‑term use of Glycosmart FB Capsule may increase the risk of eye problems such as glaucoma or cataracts and may slightly weaken bones. Regular check‑ups can help detect these issues early.

faq.question: Can I stop using Glycosmart FB Capsule once I feel better?

faq.question: What should I avoid while using Glycosmart FB Capsule?
faq.answer: While using Glycosmart FB Capsule, avoid exposure to people with contagious infections such as chickenpox or measles, as the steroid part of this medicine can reduce your resistance to infections.

faq.question: Who should not take GlyNASE Tablet?

faq.question: Can I skip GlyNASE Tablet for a few days?

faq.question: How long should Glynium Respicap be taken?

faq.question: Can Glynium Respicap inhalation cause difficulty in urination?

This condition can cause difficulty in urination, painful urination, frequent urination, or dribbling of urine. Inform the doctor if you already have any such problems before starting the treatment or if you experienced any problems during the treatment.

faq.question: Can Glynium Respicap inhalation cause difficulty in vision?

description:
Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR is used to treat and prevent heart-related chest pain (angina).
Angina occurs when the heart muscle is not getting enough blood.
This medicine works by relaxing and widening blood vessels so blood can flow more easily to the heart.
Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR should be taken in the dose and duration as advised by your doctor.
It may be taken with or without food, preferably at a fixed time each day.
Do not consume more than the recommended dose, as this may have harmful effects on your body.
You can develop tolerance to this medicine over time, which means that the same dose becomes less effective.
You have to stick to a really specific dosing schedule to prevent this from happening.The most common side effect of this medicine is a headache, which may be severe.
This can sometimes be helped by drinking plenty of fluids and avoiding alcohol.
You may also experience lightheadedness, which could increase your risk of having a fall.
There are other, rarer side effects, some of them serious.
Ask your doctor and read the leaflet that comes with the medicine to make sure you are keeping safe.Do not use this medicine if you are taking medicines to treat high blood pressure in your lungs (pulmonary hypertension), erectile dysfunction, or if you have anemia or glaucoma (increased pressure inside the eye).
Always tell your doctor what other health conditions you have and what other medicines you are taking.
It is best not to drink alcohol with this medicine as it increases some of the side effects.
If you are affected by dizziness, avoid driving.
If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, ask your doctor before taking this medicine.

faq.question: Can I take sildenafil if I am taking Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR?
faq.answer: No, you should not take sildenafil if you are taking Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR. Taking these two medicines together can cause an excessive fall in blood pressure, which may even be life-threatening.

faq.question: What effect does Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR have on blood pressure?
faq.answer: Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR decreases the blood pressure by relaxing the blood vessels, but is not recommended for the treatment of high blood pressure. The drop in blood pressure may cause lightheadedness, especially when changing your position suddenly.

faq.question: Does the effect of Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR wear off after some time?
faq.answer: Yes, excessive use of Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR may cause tolerance, which means that Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR may lose its effectiveness on you. Therefore, usually the doctors prescribe the smallest dose required for effective relief of an acute angina attack. This helps maintain the effectiveness of Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR.

faq.question: What does too much Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR do?
faq.answer: Excess Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR may result in low blood pressure, sweating, nausea, vomiting, headache, weak and fast pulse. It may also cause weakness, lightheadedness on standing, and the patient might even faint. The patient will require emergency medical treatment in such a case.

faq.question: Can I stop using Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR as I feel better now?
faq.answer: Stopping Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR suddenly may bring on attacks of angina, especially if you have been using it for several weeks or more. Talk to your doctor, who will advise you to reduce the dose gradually over 4 to 6 weeks before you stop using it completely.

faq.question: Does Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR stop heart attacks?
faq.answer: Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR is prescribed to prevent attacks of heart-related chest pain (angina) in patients with coronary artery disease. In this disease, the blood vessels (coronary arteries) that supply blood to the heart become narrowed, because of which the heart has to work harder to get enough oxygen. Glyrate 2.6 Tablet CR prevents angina by relaxing the blood vessels so that the heart does not have to work very hard. Also, relaxation of the coronary arteries increases the oxygen supply to the heart.

description:
Glyson-MF Tablet belongs to a category of medicines known as anti-diabetic drugs.
It is a combination of two medicines used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults.
It helps control blood sugar levels in people with diabetes.
Glyson-MF Tablet should be taken with food.
Take it regularly at the same time each day to get the most benefit.
Your doctor will decide what dose is best for you and this may change from time to time according to how it is working according to your blood sugar levels.Keep taking this medicine, even if you feel well or your blood sugar levels are controlled.
If you stop it without consulting your doctor, your blood sugar levels could rise and put you at risk of kidney damage, blindness, nerve problems and loss of limbs.
Remember that it is only part of a treatment program that should also include a healthy diet, regular exercise, and weight reduction as advised by your doctor.
Your lifestyle plays a big part in controlling diabetes.Some people may experience dizziness, headache, diarrhea, or upper respiratory tract infections while taking Glyson-MF Tablet.
These effects are usually mild and tend to improve as the body adjusts to treatment.
If any side effects persist or become bothersome, it is advised to consult a doctor.You should not take it if you have type 1 diabetes mellitus, if you have diabetic ketoacidosis (high levels of acid in your blood), or if you have severe kidney or liver disease.
Before taking this medicine, tell your doctor if you have ever had heart disease.
It may not be suitable.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.
Your blood sugar levels should be checked regularly and your doctor may also advise blood tests to monitor your blood cell counts and liver function.

faq.question: What is Glyson-MF Tablet?
faq.answer: Glyson-MF Tablet is a combination of two medicines: Glipizide and Metformin. This medicine is used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). It improves the blood glucose levels in adults when taken along with proper diet and regular exercise. Glipizide lowers the blood glucose levels by increasing the release of insulin from the pancreas. Metformin works by lowering the glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity. This combination is not indicated for the treatment of type 1 DM.

faq.question: What are the possible side effects of Glyson-MF Tablet?
faq.answer: The use of Glyson-MF Tablet is associated with common side effects like hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level), altered taste, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache and upper respiratory tract infection. Its use can also lead to serious but rare side effects like lactic acidosis. On long-term use, it can also lead to Vitamin B12 deficiency.

faq.question: Can the use of Glyson-MF Tablet cause hypoglycemia?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glyson-MF Tablet can cause hypoglycemia (low blood sugar level). Symptoms of hypoglycemia include nausea, headache, irritability, hunger, sweating, dizziness, fast heart rate and feeling anxious or shaky. It happens more often if you miss or delay your food, drink alcohol, over-exercise or take other antidiabetic medicine along with it. So, regular monitoring of the blood sugar level is important. Always carry some glucose tablets, honey or fruit juice with you.

faq.question: Can the use of Glyson-MF Tablet cause lactic acidosis?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glyson-MF Tablet can lead to lactic acidosis. It is a medical emergency which is caused by increased levels of lactic acid in the blood. It is also known as MALA (Metformin associated lactic acidosis). It is a rare side effect associated with the use of metformin and therefore, it is avoided in patients with underlying kidney disease, old age patients or who take large amounts of alcohol. Symptoms of lactic acidosis may include muscle pain or weakness, dizziness, tiredness, feeling of cold in arms and legs, difficulty in breathing, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or slow heart rate. If you have these symptoms, stop taking Glyson-MF Tablet and immediately consult your doctor.

faq.question: Can the use of Glyson-MF Tablet lead to Vitamin B12 deficiency?
faq.answer: Yes, the use of Glyson-MF Tablet can cause Vitamin B12 deficiency on long-term use. It interferes with absorption of Vitamin B12 in the stomach. If untreated, it may cause anemia and nerve problems and the patient can feel a tingling sensation and numbness in the hands and feet, weakness, urinary problems, change in mental status and difficulty in maintaining balance (ataxia). To avoid such problems, some researchers suggest an intake of Vitamin B12 from outside sources at least once every year.

faq.question: Are there any specific conditions in which Glyson-MF Tablet should not to be taken?
faq.answer: The use of Glyson-MF Tablet should be avoided in patients with known allergy to any of the components or excipients of this medicine. It should also be avoided in patients with moderate to severe kidney disease and in patients with underlying metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis.

faq.question: Is it safe to take alcohol while I am also taking Glyson-MF Tablet?
faq.answer: No, it is not safe to take Glyson-MF Tablet along with alcohol, as it may lower your low blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia) and can increase the chances of lactic acidosis.

faq.question: What are the instructions for storage and disposal of Glyson-MF Tablet?
faq.answer: Keep this medicine in the container or the pack it came in, tightly closed. Store it according to the instructions mentioned on the pack or label. Dispose of the unused medicine. Make sure it is not consumed by pets, children and other people.

faq.question: Does GP 0.5 Tablet make you sleepy?
